question: The average of 13 numbers is 22. If each number is multiplied by 3, what will be the new average?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If each number in a given set is multiplied by a certain constant, the new average is simply the old average multiplied by the same constant.

New Average = Old Average × Constant

New Average = 22 × 3 = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average of 13 numbers = 22

Constant multiplier for each number = 3

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 Property of Averages
 
 Original Average:
 
 22
 
 
• 
 

 Each number × 3
 
 New Average:
 
 66 (i.e. 22 × 3)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of the original 13 numbers = Average × Total numbers

⇒ Original Sum = 22 × 13 = 286

⇒ When each individual number is multiplied by 3, the total sum is also multiplied by 3.

⇒ New Sum = Original Sum × 3

⇒ New Sum = 286 × 3 = 858

⇒ New Average = New Sum ÷ Total numbers

⇒ New Average = 858 ÷ 13 = 66

**∴ The correct answer is 66.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Addition and Subtraction Property

If a constant value 'k' is added to or subtracted from each observation in a dataset, the new average becomes (Old Average + k) or (Old Average − k).

Multiplication and Division Property

If each observation is multiplied or divided by a non-zero constant 'k', the new average becomes (Old Average × k) or (Old Average ÷ k).

Combined Average

If group 1 has n₁ items with average A₁ and group 2 has n₂ items with average A₂, the Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).
